verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, according to the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus,
verses.1:2: to Timothy, beloved child: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.1:3: I give thanks to God, whom I serve from my ancestors with a pure conscience, as I continually keep remembrance of you in my petitions night and day,
verses.1:4: longing to see you, remembering your tears, so that I may be filled with joy,
verses.1:5: recalling to mind the sincere faith within you, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am persuaded that it is in you also.
verses.1:6: For this reason I remind you to rekindle the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands;
verses.1:7: for God did not give us a spirit of cowardice, but of power, love, and self-discipline.
verses.1:8: Therefore do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me His prisoner, but share in suffering hardship for the gospel according to the power of God,
verses.1:9: who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to His own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before eternal times,
verses.1:10: yet has now been made manifest through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus, who rendered death powerless and brought life and incorruptibility to light through the gospel,
verses.1:11: for which I was appointed a herald and an apostle and a teacher.
verses.1:12: For this reason I also suffer these things, yet I am not ashamed; for I know whom I have trusted, and I am persuaded that He is able to guard my deposit until that day.
verses.1:13: Hold the pattern of sound words that you heard from me, in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus;
verses.1:14: guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
verses.1:15: You know this, that all those in Asia turned away from me, among whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes.
verses.1:16: May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain;
verses.1:17: instead, when he was in Rome, he searched diligently for me and found me—
verses.1:18: may the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day—and you know very well all the ways he served in Ephesus.
verses.2:1: You therefore, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
verses.2:2: And the things that you heard from me in the presence of many witnesses, entrust these to faithful people who will be competent to teach others also.
verses.2:3: Share in suffering hardship as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
verses.2:4: No one serving as a soldier gets entangled in the affairs of everyday life, so that he may please the one who enlisted him.
verses.2:5: And also, if anyone competes as an athlete, he is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.
verses.2:6: The hardworking farmer must be the first to share in the crops.
verses.2:7: Consider what I am saying, for the Lord will give you understanding in everything.
verses.2:8: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, of the offspring of David, according to my gospel,
verses.2:9: in which I suffer hardship to the point of chains as a criminal; yet the word of God is not chained.
verses.2:10: For this reason I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they also may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.
verses.2:11: The saying is trustworthy: For if we died with Him, we will also live with Him;
verses.2:12: if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He will also deny us;
verses.2:13: if we are faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.
verses.2:14: Remind them of these things, solemnly charging them before God not to dispute about words, which is useful for nothing, to the ruin of the hearers.
verses.2:15: Make every effort to present yourself to God as approved, an unashamed worker, properly handling the word of truth.
verses.2:16: But avoid irreverent empty chatter, for they will advance further into ungodliness,
verses.2:17: and their talk will spread like gangrene; among whom are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
verses.2:18: who have missed the mark regarding the truth, saying that the resurrection has already taken place, and they are overturning the faith of some.
verses.2:19: Nevertheless, the firm foundation of God stands, bearing this seal: "The Lord knows those who are His," and, "Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from unrighteousness."
verses.2:20: Now in a large house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and earthenware, and some are for honor and others for dishonor.
verses.2:21: Therefore, if anyone cleanses himself from these, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work.
verses.2:22: Flee youthful desires, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.
verses.2:23: But refuse foolish and ignorant controversies, knowing that they breed quarrels.
verses.2:24: And a servant of the Lord must not quarrel, but be gentle toward all, able to teach, patient when wronged,
verses.2:25: with gentleness instructing those who stand in opposition, so that perhaps God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth,
verses.2:26: and they may come to their senses out of the snare of the devil, having been captured alive by him to do his will.
verses.3:1: But know this, that in the last days harsh times will set in.
verses.3:2: For people will be lovers of self, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, unholy,
verses.3:3: heartless, irreconcilable, slanderous, without self-control, brutal, not loving what is good,
verses.3:4: treacherous, reckless, puffed up, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,
verses.3:5: holding an outward form of godliness, yet having denied its power; turn away from these people also.
verses.3:6: For among them are those who creep into households and take captive weak women weighed down with sins, led along by various desires,
verses.3:7: always learning and never able to come to a knowledge of the truth.
verses.3:8: Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these also oppose the truth—people corrupted in mind, disqualified regarding the faith.
verses.3:9: Yet they will not advance any further, for their folly will be completely plain to all, just as theirs also became.
verses.3:10: You, however, have closely followed my teaching, my conduct, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, my endurance,
verses.3:11: my persecutions, and my sufferings, such as happened to me at Antioch, at Iconium, and at Lystra—what persecutions I endured! And out of them all the Lord rescued me.
verses.3:12: And indeed, all who desire to live in a godly manner in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
verses.3:13: But evil people and impostors will advance to what is worse, deceiving and being deceived.
verses.3:14: You, however, remain in the things you have learned and become convinced of, knowing from whom you learned them,
verses.3:15: and that from infancy you have known the sacred writings, which are able to make you wise for salvation through the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:16: All Scripture is God-breathed and beneficial for teaching, for rebuke, for correction, and for discipline in righteousness,
verses.3:17: so that the man of God may be proficient, thoroughly equipped for every good work.
verses.4:1: I solemnly charge you before God and Christ Jesus, who is about to judge the living and the dead, and by His appearing and His kingdom:
verses.4:2: proclaim the word; stand ready in season and out of season; convict, rebuke, exhort, with all patience and teaching.
verses.4:3: For a time will come when they will not tolerate sound teaching, but in accordance with their own desires they will pile up teachers for themselves, having ears that itch,
verses.4:4: and they will turn their ears away from the truth, and will turn aside to myths.
verses.4:5: But you, be clear-minded in everything, bear hardship, do the work of an evangelist, fully carry out your ministry.
verses.4:6: For I am already being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of my departure has arrived.
verses.4:7: I have contended in the good contest, I have completed the race, I have kept the faith.
verses.4:8: From now on, the crown of righteousness is stored up for me, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will give to me on that day—and not only to me, but also to all those who have loved His appearing.
verses.4:9: Be diligent to come to me quickly.
verses.4:10: For Demas deserted me, having loved the present age, and went to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
verses.4:11: Luke alone is with me. Take Mark along and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for ministry.
verses.4:12: But I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
verses.4:13: When you come, bring the cloak that I left in Troas with Carpus, as well as the scrolls, especially the parchments.
verses.4:14: Alexander the metalworker did much evil to me—the Lord will repay him according to his works—
verses.4:15: against whom you also should be on guard, for he strongly opposed our words.
verses.4:16: At my first defense no one appeared beside me, but all deserted me—may it not be counted against them—
verses.4:17: but the Lord stood beside me and empowered me, so that through me the proclamation might be fully carried out and all the Gentiles might hear; and I was rescued from the mouth of a lion.
verses.4:18: The Lord will rescue me from every evil work and will save me into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.4:19: Greet Prisca and Aquila and Onesiphorus's household.
verses.4:20: Erastus stayed in Corinth, but I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.
verses.4:21: Be diligent to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers.
verses.4:22: May the Lord be with your spirit. May grace be with you.

notes.1:7: Greek pneuma can refer either to a human disposition ("a spirit") or to the Holy Spirit; sophronismos denotes self-discipline, moderation, or sound judgment.
notes.1:12: "My deposit" (ten paratheken mou) may mean either what Paul has entrusted to God (such as his soul or life) or what God has entrusted to Paul (the gospel ministry; compare 1:14).
notes.1:18: Paul's wish that Onesiphorus find mercy "on that day" (the day of judgment) and his greeting only to Onesiphorus's household (1:16; 4:19) have led many interpreters to infer that Onesiphorus had died, though others view him simply as absent.
notes.2:14: The Greek text here reads "before God" (tou Theou); some manuscripts read "before the Lord" (tou kyriou).
notes.2:15: "Properly handling" translates orthotomounta, literally "cutting straight," used metaphorically for accurately expounding and applying the word of truth.
notes.2:19: The first quotation echoes Numbers 16:5 in the Septuagint; the second draws on Old Testament language such as Numbers 16:26 and Isaiah 26:13.
notes.2:26: The pronouns "by him" (autou) and "his will" (ekeinou) are grammatically ambiguous: both may refer to the devil, or "him" may refer to the devil (or to the Lord's servant) while "his" refers to God ("to do His will").
notes.3:8: Jannes and Jambres are the traditional Jewish names for the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses in Exodus 7:11, 22.
notes.3:14: The pronoun "whom" (tinon) is plural in Greek, encompassing Timothy's mother and grandmother (1:5) as well as Paul.
notes.3:16: The clause lacks an explicit verb "is"; while most interpreters take both adjectives as predicates ("All Scripture is God-breathed and beneficial"), it can also be construed attributively ("Every God-breathed scripture is also beneficial").
notes.4:7: The Greek terms ἀγών ("contest" or "fight") and δρόμος ("race") draw on athletic imagery that continues into the victor's crown (στέφανος, wreath) in verse 8.
notes.4:10: The Greek critical text reads Γαλατίαν ("Galatia"), though several early manuscripts read Γαλλίαν ("Gaul").
notes.4:14: The Greek critical text reads the future indicative ἀποδώσει ("will repay"), expressing a statement of certainty rather than the optative wish ("may he repay") found in later manuscripts.
notes.4:22: The Greek pronoun shifts from singular σου ("your spirit") to plural ὑμῶν ("with you"), extending the final blessing to the wider congregation; later manuscripts also add "Jesus Christ" after "the Lord" and "Amen" at the end.
